threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the pole' refers to a light fixture and not the train station. Watch out; the locals will side-eye you for that one!
Caught a bloke singing opera on the 333 last night, completely lit. Tourists loved it, but the driver looked ready to jump off the bus.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted the old lady in the park arguing with a pigeon over a pretzel crumb. That’s when it hit me—this place has character.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a spontaneous karaoke bar in a back alley, just a worn-out mic and a crowd of locals belting out 90s hits under fairy lights.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they complain about the BART breaks being too hot to handle, but still choose it over Muni every time.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw someone juggle while waiting for the 31, and a guy in a suit ignored it completely, glued to his phone. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars close early, but the locals know the best ones get lively after midnight, filled with hidden gems and late-night tapas.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They'll be the ones struggling with 'escudella' pronunciation while trying to order it at the local eatery.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'cabbie' instead of just 'the taxi'. The locals are all about proper Uber etiquette now.
Last night on the 333, a bloke serenaded us with Whitney Houston. The driver just rolled his eyes but we all clapped. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a couple of kids trading Pokémon cards at the bus stop while an old man sang opera nearby—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a street vendor selling vegan döner at 3 AM, surrounded by hipsters and late-night partygoers. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they instinctively dodge the BART delays, while newcomers stand confused at the Civic Center station.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 31 Hayes trying to haggle with a bus driver over fare while simultaneously offering a bag of avocados. Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think we all speak perfect English. While many do, a simple 'hola' goes a long way in making connections here.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by how they hold their metro ticket; tightly clutched in their palm, unlike locals who slip it casually into their pocket.
